g.text: Extends WatchDog (an independent LLM monitor for agentic robotic assembly) onto a blockchain.
The executor cannot verify itself; an independent WatchDog with its own observation channel can, and the chain makes that testimony permanent.

text.tspan: — Merkle roots anchored on-chain, raw data off-chain
— every claim and verdict signed by a known agent
— challenge window, neutral judge, human audit

g.text: Signed by customer + operator · only assigned keys commit/rule
• Executors never choose their own inspector
• The crew never chooses its judge
• Executor and WatchDog evidence never merged
• Real-time advice stays off-chain; hash committed
• Judge knows its rulings are randomly audited
own manifest · own key · own tx
own channel · own key · own tx
two roots · specVersion · advice hash · signed transactions
• Raw data kept until window closes
per step & role: claim/verdict, specVersion, one 32-byte Merkle root
chain boundary: raw data never goes on-chain
kept at least until the window closes
kept at least until the window closes
raw streams in a content-addressed store: store/<keccak256(chunk)>
Merkle commitment, one tree per (session, role, step)
path recomputed from L2 up to root
OpenZeppelin MerkleProof.verify; only the proven chunk is revealed
store · manifests · CLIs: commit, prove, verify
